source: Domain research: FRC data logging, deterministic match replay, 3D/mechanism visualization (August 2026 state of the art). Primary sources: docs.advantagekit.org + AdvantageKit GitHub source at tag v26.0.2 and main, docs.advantagescope.org + AdvantageScope GitHub docs/bundledAssets, wpilibsuite/frc-docs source .rst, allwpilib struct.adoc + datalog.adoc + epilogue-runtime source at tag v2026.2.1, doglog.dev docs source, CTRE Phoenix 6 docs, REVLib docs, Chief Delphi thread JSON APIs, and FRC 6328's RobotCode2026Public robot code.
summary: As of Aug 2026 the FRC logging/visualization stack has consolidated hard around two artifacts: the WPILOG binary file format (v1.0, spec at allwpilib/datalog/doc/datalog.adoc) and AdvantageScope as the universal viewer. There are exactly three live Java logging frameworks — AdvantageKit 26.0.2 (BSD-3, Littleton Robotics; the only *deterministic* replay framework), WPILib Epilogue (annotation/codegen, `edu.wpi.first.epilogue`, in-tree, no replay), and DogLog 2026.5.0 (Team 581; imperative `DogLog.log()` over DataLogManager+NT4, no replay). Monologue is dead — last commit 2024-06-21, last release v1.0.0-beta6 (2024-03-09), no 2025/2026 vendordep; do not target it. AdvantageKit's replay is genuinely deterministic (synchronized timestamps injected into WPILib, all inputs captured behind IO layers) and runs ~50x real-time; CTRE's Hoot Replay is explicitly non-deterministic and diverges within seconds of auto per 6328's published side-by-side. The killer replay use case is not "change the code" — it's "add a `Logger.recordOutput()` line for a variable you never logged, rebuild, replay, and see its value during match 42," plus attaching a debugger to replay. AdvantageScope 2026 (v26.0.2) shipped unit-aware line graphs, 2-4x faster log download (SFTP→FTP), `.revlog` support, CSV import, and YZ-plane Mechanism2d projection; the 3D asset format is a folder named `Robot_NAME` containing `model.glb` + `model_0.glb`…`model_N.glb` + a `config.json` with `rotations`/`position`/`cameras`/`components[].zeroedRotations`/`zeroedPosition`, and articulated mechanisms animate by publishing a `Pose3d[]` of robot-relative component poses. The real 2026 pain is roboRIO CPU: multiple teams on Chief Delphi hit 100-600ms loop times with the AdvantageKit vision+swerve templates, and the fixes were always "log fewer/smaller fields" or "you left simMode on." Loom over everything: WPILib 2027 renames `edu.wpi.first.*`→`org.wpilib.*`, `frc::`→`wpi::`, deletes Shuffleboard and SmartDashboard entirely, adds Commands v3, moves the FRC field origin to field-center/+X-away-from-red, and ships a new FIRST Driver Station that writes WPILog and serves AdvantageScope Lite from its own web server.

landscape.doesWell: The only deterministic log-replay framework in FRC. Captures ALL inputs behind IO interfaces, injects a synchronized per-cycle timestamp into WPILib so `Timer.getTimestamp()` replays exactly, and re-runs the identical control logic in sim. Auto-logs DriverStation + all HID, alerts, console (incl. exceptions in 2026), VH-109 radio status every ~5s, PDP/PDH currents, SystemStats (incl. NT client list, new 2026), and a full perf breakdown (`LoggedRobot/FullCycleMS`, `UserCodeMs`, `LogPeriodicMS`, `GCTimeMS`, `GCCount`, `Logger/QueuedCycle`). `@AutoLog` codegen generates `toLog`/`fromLog`. Records, enums, structs, protobufs, 2D arrays, Color (hex triplet), Measure/unit metadata, LoggedMechanism2d all supported. `Logger.recordOutput` has ~60 overloads incl. `BooleanSupplier` (so `Trigger`s log directly). Replay Watch (`./gradlew replayWatch`) re-runs replay on every file save and pushes results into AdvantageScope live. License is plain BSD-3-Clause (the 2023-era restrictive license is gone).
landscape.gaps: Requires you to restructure every subsystem into IO interface + inputs object — highest adoption cost of the three. 'Replay bubble': modified outputs cannot affect replayed inputs, so you cannot re-simulate a different control decision, only re-derive outputs from the same inputs. Breaks on any non-deterministic source: `Timer.getMonotonicTimestamp()`, raw NT reads, `Math.random`, filesystem reads, iteration over unordered collections, multithreading, and 'large hardware libraries that bypass IO layers' (i.e. CTRE SwerveDrivetrain, YAGSL). `DriverStation.waitForDsConnection` is incompatible. Vendor CAN signal loggers (URCL, hoot) are logged for convenience but explicitly NOT available in replay. Real-world CPU cost is the #1 complaint: teams report 80-600ms loop times with the stock vision/swerve templates. No 2027 templates yet.
landscape.version2026: v26.0.2 (2026-03-19, WPILib 2026.2.1). Vendordep https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit/releases/latest/download/AdvantageKit.json, frcYear "2026", maven https://frcmaven.wpi.edu/artifactory/littletonrobotics-mvn-release/, artifacts org.littletonrobotics.akit:akit-java + akit-wpilibio (JNI, athena/linuxx86-64/linuxarm64/osxuniversal/windowsx86-64). 2027 line is v27.0.0-alpha-4 (2026-06-26), Systemcore-alpha only.

landscape.doesWell: Universal FRC log viewer/analyzer. Reads .wpilog, .dslog/.dsevents (auto-pairs them), .hoot (behind CTRE EULA prompt), .revlog, Road Runner .log, .csv, legacy .rlog. Opens multiple logs at once with automatic timestamp alignment (fields land under Log0/Log1/…). Tabs: unit-aware Line Graph (2026 redesign, integration/differentiation with correct derived units), 2D Field, 3D Field (Cinematic/Standard/Low-Power render modes, orbit-field / orbit-robot / driver-station / fixed-camera modes, Camera Override pose for turret-mounted cams), Swerve, Mechanism, Joysticks, Table, Console, Points, Metadata, Statistics (histogram + mean/median/mode/geometric/harmonic/quadratic mean, stdev, MAD, IQR, skewness, percentiles, with Reference/Relative-Error/Absolute-Error child fields), and Video (local file / YouTube / The Blue Alliance auto-match-lookup with TBA API key; auto-syncs off score overlays, FFmpeg required). Timeline selection is synchronized across every tab — click a moment on the graph and the 3D field, video, and console all jump there. Tuning mode publishes edits back to NT. Export to CSV/WPILOG/MCAP (MCAP → Foxglove). Custom assets folder can point at a folder inside your repo so robot models are version-controlled with code.
landscape.gaps: 3D component setup is fiddly enough that the docs themselves warn it is 'complex and time-consuming' and steer you to Mechanism2d instead. Asset config is hand-authored JSON with trial-and-error rotation/position calibration — no GUI calibrator. XR is iOS/iPadOS only, no Android/Quest, and heatmaps + swerve module velocities are unsupported in XR. Video sync auto-detection only works on match videos with score overlays. No scripting/plugin API, no headless/CI mode, no query language over a log. No built-in 'diff two logs' view (you can overlay them, but no automated field-by-field divergence report).
landscape.version2026: v26.0.2 (2026-04-25). 2027 line at v27.0.0-alpha-5 (2026-06-26). 2026 highlights: unit-aware line graph, FTP log download (3.2x faster under high RIO CPU: 25→80 Mb/s), subfolder downloads (for CTRE Signal Logger's folder-per-session layout), .revlog + CSV import, YZ-plane Mechanism2d on 3D field, 3D anti-aliasing, Windows 11 translucent sidebar.

landscape.doesWell: Zero-config on-robot recording: `DataLogManager.start()` records every NetworkTables change. All file IO happens on a background thread, so the hot path is 'mainly a mutex acquisition and copying the data.' Auto file management: writes to `logs` on a FAT32 USB stick if attached, else `/home/lvuser/logs`; names files `WPILib_TBD_{random}.wpilog` until DS connects, then `WPILib_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss.wpilog`, then `WPILib_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss_{event}_{match}.wpilog` once FMS supplies a match number. Deletes never-DS-connected logs on startup, and prunes oldest-first when under 50 MB free (floor of 10 files). `DriverStation.startDataLog(DataLogManager.getLog())` adds DS control + joystick data. `DataLogManager.log()` doubles as `System.out.println`. Writes roboRIO UTC `systemTime` every ~5s for rough sync to DS logs and match video. Format is documented, tiny, and trivially parseable: 8-byte header `57 50 49 4c 4f 47 00 01 …`, then records of {header-length bitfield, 1-4B entry ID, 1-4B payload size, 1-8B µs timestamp, payload}, little-endian, no ordering requirement.
landscape.gaps: No replay. No change detection in raw `LogEntry.append()` — every call writes a record, dedup is the caller's job. `DataLog` is write-only and `DataLogReader` is read-only; no round-trip. Metadata is a free-form (conventionally JSON) string. Captured DS/joystick data cannot be mirrored to NetworkTables (a DataLogManager limitation DogLog documents explicitly).
landscape.version2026: WPILib 2026.2.2 is the current release; `edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.DataLogManager`, `edu.wpi.first.util.datalog.{DataLog,BooleanLogEntry,DoubleLogEntry,StringLogEntry}`. In 2027 these move to `org.wpilib.system.DataLogManager` / `org.wpilib.datalog.DataLog`, and log paths move to `/home/systemcore/logs` or `/u/logs`.

landscape.doesWell: Compile-time annotation processor — no reflection at runtime. `@Logged` on a class generates a `ClassSpecificLogger` for it; the generated `Epilogue` class is the entry point. `Epilogue.bind(this)` on a `TimedRobot` schedules logging at loop rate but phase-offset by half a period so it doesn't collide with control loops. Logs all public+private non-static fields and all zero-arg public methods of loggable type. Supports primitives, String, anything `StructSerializable` (and arrays/List/Set of them), `Measure` (as base-unit double), `Sendable`, and all four primitive suppliers — which means `Trigger` fields log as booleans for free. `@Logged(name=..., importance=..., loggingPeriod=..., loggingPeriodOffset=...)`, `@NotLogged` to exclude, `@CustomLoggerFor(VendorMotor.class)` to log third-party types. Backends in `edu.wpi.first.epilogue.logging`: `NTEpilogueBackend` (default), `FileBackend`, `LazyBackend`, `MultiBackend`, `NestedBackend`, `NullBackend`. Configurable `root`, `minimumImportance`, and an `ErrorHandler` so logging exceptions cannot crash the robot. Self-reports cost to `/Epilogue/Stats/Last Run`.
landscape.gaps: No replay. Java only. No tunable values, no unit metadata (per DogLog's comparison table). Uses the *declared* type, not the runtime type — so an IO-interface field logs with the interface's config, not the impl's. Nulls are unloggable and throw NPE into your error handler. **`Mechanism2d` is explicitly NOT supported** ('do not implement the Sendable interface in a way that is compatible with annotation logging'). Docs warn the CPU cost is from re-querying CAN devices in the logged getters, not from logging itself.
landscape.version2026: In-tree with WPILib 2026.x; package `edu.wpi.first.epilogue` (confirmed against allwpilib tag v2026.2.1). 2027 adds reflection for non-public superclass fields, protobuf-serializable types, and backend time/memory optimizations.

landscape.doesWell: Simplest possible surface: `DogLog.log("Arm/Position", value)` and you're done, no setup boilerplate. Thin wrapper over WPILib DataLogManager + NT4, so it inherits WPILib's performance and stability rather than reinventing primitives. Unit metadata as String, `Unit`, or `Measure`. `DogLogOptions().withCaptureDs(true).withLogExtras(true).withCaptureConsole(true).withNtTunables(...)` — and `ntTunables` defaults to **ignoring NT tunables when FMS-attached**, which is exactly the competition-safe default. `DogLog.setPdh(new PowerDistribution())` adds PDH currents/battery/CAN/radio. Genuinely differentiated features Rootstock should copy: a **faults system** (`DogLog.logFault(name)` / `logFault(enum)` / `decreaseFault` / `clearFault` / `faultsLogged()`) that auto-raises WPILib persistent Alerts and publishes `Robot/Faults/Counts/<name>`, `Robot/Faults/Seen`, `Robot/Faults/Active`; and profiling helpers `DogLog.timestamp(key)`, `DogLog.time(key)` / `DogLog.timeEnd(key)`.
landscape.gaps: No replay, ever — that is the deliberate design line. No IO-layer discipline, so nothing stops you from reading hardware mid-cycle. Java only. Docs explicitly warn against mixing it with another logging library ('you will almost certainly encounter bugs'). The FAQ itself concedes the failure mode: at some point 'the roboRIO simply can't keep up with the volume of data being logged.'
landscape.version2026: 2026.5.0 (2026-02-11) is the last 2026-season release. Current is 2027.1.0 (2026-05-31); vendordep https://doglog.dev/vendordep.json declares wpilibYear "2027_alpha5", com.github.jonahsnider:doglog:2027.0.0 via jitpack. Note the 2027 docs already import `org.wpilib.units.Units`.

landscape.doesWell: Historically: the annotation-logging library that Epilogue was modeled on; `@Log`/`@Log.NT` on fields and methods, logged to NT and/or DataLog.
landscape.gaps: **DEAD — do not target.** Repo last pushed 2024-06-21; latest release is v1.0.0-beta6 dated 2024-03-09; no 2025, 2026, or 2027 release or vendordep exists. It was effectively absorbed into WPILib as Epilogue. DogLog's own 2026 comparison table lists only DogLog, AdvantageKit, and Epilogue as 'the three main solutions for logging' — Monologue is not mentioned.
landscape.integrationShape: N/A — Rootstock should not integrate or mention Monologue except to tell migrating teams to move to Epilogue or DogLog.

landscape.doesWell: SignalLogger captures every device status signal at its configured update frequency with **CAN RX timestamps**, in a background process that is 'not affected by the timing of the main robot loop or Java GC.' Enabled by default on roboRIO; auto-starts 1s after enable or 5s after DS connect. `SignalLogger.setPath(String)`, `.start()`, `.stop()`, `.enableAutoLogging(boolean)`, `.writeDouble(...)`, `.writeStruct(...)`. One file per CAN bus, grouped into a subfolder per program-start datetime (AdvantageScope 2026 added subfolder-group download specifically for this). Auto-deletes old logs at 50 MB free, stops logging at 5 MB. Converts to WPILOG/MCAP via Tuner X Log Extractor or the `owlet` CLI. AdvantageScope opens .hoot directly after a one-time CTRE EULA acceptance.
landscape.gaps: Hoot Replay is **non-deterministic** and requires a Pro-licensed device in the log. 6328 published a direct comparison showing Hoot Replay diverging completely from the real robot within a few seconds of auto even in a best-case, hand-compensated 5x run — and at 5x it is still ~10x slower than AdvantageKit's ~50x. Only one hoot log replayable at a time; configs and control requests are ignored during replay; logs must load before devices are constructed. Free (non-Pro) logs export only a subset of signals. Nonstandard folder layout. Cannot be precisely time-synchronized with other sources without conversion.
landscape.version2026: Phoenix 6 26.x. Hoot Replay ships as its own vendordep that replaces hardware-attached simulation; `HootReplay.loadFile/play/pause/stop/restart/setSpeed/stepTiming/isFileLoaded/isPlaying/isFinished/waitForPlaying/getDouble/getStruct`, plus `HootAutoReplay` and `Utils.isReplay()`.

landscape.doesWell: New in 2026: REVLib ships an **official** CAN logger (`com.revrobotics.util.statuslogger`) producing `.revlog` files that AdvantageScope opens natively. URCL (Unofficial REV-Compatible Logger, by 6328) remains available for 2026 and logs Spark Max/Flex frames to NT or DataLog with CAN-RX timestamps, capturing every frame even when the status period is faster than the robot loop, at <80µs per 20ms cycle. URCL supports CAN-ID→alias maps and is the recommended SysId data source for Sparks (pass `null` as the SysId log consumer, then read `NT:/URCL/<Device>/{MotorPositionRotations, MotorVelocityRPM, AppliedOutputVoltage}`).
landscape.gaps: .revlog 'cannot be precisely synchronized to other data sources.' URCL data is explicitly **not available in AdvantageKit replay** — REV motors must still sit behind an IO layer. Most Spark status frames are **disabled by default** in 2025+ REVLib until a getter is called, so anything you don't read is silently absent from the log; you must configure `SignalsConfig` explicitly. URCL SysId logs must be round-tripped through AdvantageScope's export ('Include Generated') before the SysId analyzer will read them. REV/6328 have signaled that 2026 is a transition year and 2027 logging options are TBD.
landscape.version2026: URCL vendordep https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mechanical-Advantage/URCL/main/URCL.json; REVLib StatusLogger new in 2026.

landscape.doesWell: Simplest superstructure visualization: a 2D canvas with roots and jointed `MechanismLigament2d` segments (length, angle, color, line weight). Renders in Glass, and AdvantageScope has a dedicated Mechanism tab. Crucially, AdvantageScope can project a Mechanism2d **onto the 3D field** in either the XZ or YZ plane (YZ new in 2026) as simple boxes attached to a robot or ghost object, with the robot origin at the bottom-center of the mechanism — the docs recommend this over articulated 3D components as the 'more streamlined approach.'
landscape.gaps: Not supported by Epilogue at all. In AdvantageKit you must use `LoggedMechanism2d`/`LoggedMechanismRoot2d`/`LoggedMechanismObject2d`/`LoggedMechanismLigament2d`, not the WPILib classes. `Logger.recordOutput(key, mech)` snapshots the *current* state, so it must be called every cycle (or use `@AutoLogOutput` on the field). Boxes only — no real geometry.
landscape.version2026: WPILib 2026.2.2 / AdvantageKit 26.0.2. Verified against source: `LoggedMechanism2d.generate3dMechanism()` returns `ArrayList<Pose3d>`.

landscape.doesWell: The wire format everything agrees on. `StructPublisher<Pose3d>` / `StructArrayPublisher<Pose3d>` publish byte-packed fixed-size structs that AdvantageScope decodes natively and that carry **native unit information** — the docs call publishing via structs 'always the best way to publish data.' Struct schema is a C-like declaration string (`bool`, `char`, `int8..int64`, `uint8..uint64`, `float/float32`, `double/float64`, fixed arrays, nested structs, bitfields, enum specs), little-endian, spec v1.0. WPILOG and NT4 both carry per-entry JSON metadata, and AdvantageScope reads `"unit"`/`"units"` keys from it. Fallback unit inference from field-name suffixes (`PositionMeters`, `velocity_rad_per_sec`, `timestamp s`).
landscape.gaps: Protobuf (and custom record) logging can block **>100 ms the first time** a given type is logged — AdvantageKit's docs mandate doing the first log of such a value while disabled. Records must use only primitives/enums/struct types/nested records — no array fields — and record class names must be globally unique or they collide. NT4 traffic is bandwidth on the field; AdvantageKit's `NT4Publisher` is usually disabled when FMS-attached (6328 ship a `NoFMSNT4Publisher`).
landscape.version2026: Struct spec v1.0 (rev 0x0100). WPILOG spec v1.0 (rev 0x0100). NT3 is removed in 2027.

landscape.doesWell: Streams the 3D Field tab into AR on an iPhone/iPad with no app install (scan a QR from the desktop host; the App Store app exists only for offline use). Miniature (tabletop) or Full-Size calibration against a real field barrier; Smooth vs Low-Latency streaming modes; toggles for floor/field/robots so you can overlay vision targets or 2D mechanisms onto a *real* robot. One-tap video recording on-device. Works fully offline as long as host and client share a network.
landscape.gaps: iOS/iPadOS only, explicitly no plans for Android or headsets. Needs LiDAR devices (iPhone 12 Pro+/iPad Pro 2020+) for stability. Only one XR host session at a time. Heatmaps and swerve module velocities are unsupported in XR. Host firewall must be disabled. Demanding — complex scenes degrade.
landscape.version2026: Requires AdvantageScope desktop v4.1.0+ / v26.x and iOS 16+. 2026 release improved XR stability on iOS/iPadOS 26.
landscape.integrationShape: No robot-side API. Rootstock's only lever is asset quality: ship a `disableSimplification:false`, low-poly `model.glb` and mark critical meshes `NOSIMPLIFY` so XR stays performant.

landscape.doesWell: Browser build of AdvantageScope served off the robot / Driver Station. Assets uploaded as zips via `File > Upload Asset`. Bundles published at AdvantageScopeAssets releases: `AllAssetsDefaultFRC.zip`, `AllAssetsDefaultFTC.zip`, `AllAssetsFRC6328.zip`.
landscape.gaps: **2027-only. Not available in 2026.** Verified quote from the live docs: 'AdvantageScope Lite is only available in the 2027 (v27.x) releases of AdvantageScope on the Systemcore control system.' Omits several tab types, log formats, and related features vs desktop. The `http://localhost:6768/ascope` endpoint belongs to the new 2027 FIRST Driver Station.
landscape.version2026: Not shipped for 2026. Ships with AdvantageScope v27.x on Systemcore.
landscape.integrationShape: Design consequence for Rootstock: keep the asset pipeline emitting **zip-per-asset** so the same artifact works for both desktop custom-assets folders and 2027 Lite uploads.

landscape.doesWell: DataLogTool has a built-in SFTP client for pulling .wpilog off the robot with an optional delete-after-download, plus batch CSV export in list (timestamp,key,value) or table (one column per field) form. `DataLogReader` (Java/C++/Python, plus a pure-python `datalog.py`) lets you write custom triage scripts against the documented format. AdvantageScope auto-pairs a .dslog with its .dsevents and aligns them to the robot log.
landscape.gaps: SFTP over SSH — will not connect wirelessly while the radio firewall is up, i.e. **you cannot pull logs while the robot is on the field**. Manual, GUI-driven, one event at a time. No scheduling, no auto-pull on disable, no per-match indexing.
landscape.version2026: 2026: roboRIO paths `/home/lvuser/logs` and `/U/logs`. 2027: Systemcore paths `/home/systemcore/logs` and `/u/logs`, credentials systemcore/systemcore. The 2027 FIRST Driver Station writes its own logs in WPILog format.

landscape.doesWell: AdvantageScope exports MCAP, which opens in Foxglove — a general robotics viewer with plugin/extension APIs, layouts, and multi-source playback that AdvantageScope lacks. Useful escape hatch for teams that want custom panels or to correlate with non-FRC data.
landscape.gaps: No FRC field models, no swerve/mechanism/joystick tabs, no .dslog/.hoot/.revlog support, no AdvantageKit awareness. Export is one-way and lossy relative to AdvantageScope's generated-field handling.
landscape.version2026: MCAP export present in AdvantageScope v26.x.
landscape.integrationShape: Document as an export path only; do not build on it.

landscape.doesWell: Deterministic log replay for RobotPy/Python, called out by the AdvantageKit docs as the Python member of the deterministic-replay category alongside AdvantageKit.
landscape.gaps: Not Java; irrelevant to Rootstock's target stack except as evidence that the IO-layer + synchronized-timestamp architecture is the accepted pattern for deterministic replay.
landscape.version2026: Referenced in AdvantageKit 2026 docs; UNVERIFIED as to its own version/maturity — I did not fetch the repo.

capabilities.capability: Replay Determinism Guard — compile-time + runtime detection of code that will silently break AdvantageKit replay
capabilities.whyItMatters: Replay is AdvantageKit's whole value proposition and it fails *silently*: a small team adds `Math.random()`, a raw `SmartDashboard.getNumber()`, a `HashMap` iteration, or a vendor swerve library that bypasses the IO layer, and their replay outputs quietly stop matching reality. The AdvantageKit docs list these hazards and then say only 'we recommend regularly testing out log replay during development' — i.e. the enforcement is left entirely to team discipline. Elite teams have the discipline; a small team does not. Automating this is the single highest-leverage thing Rootstock can do in this domain and nothing today does it.
capabilities.prerequisites: AdvantageKit as the logging backend. Java 17 annotation processor (same javac plugin mechanism `@AutoLog` and Epilogue already use). Requires a curated hazard list — start from docs.advantagekit.org/getting-started/common-issues/non-deterministic-data-sources.

capabilities.capability: Replay-diff CI harness — `./gradlew replayVerify` runs a log through replay headlessly and reports RealOutputs vs ReplayOutputs divergence
capabilities.whyItMatters: 6328 proves replay fidelity by *eyeballing* overlaid graphs (their own log-replay-comparison page is literally screenshots of blue vs yellow traces). A small team will never do that consistently. Turning 'is my replay trustworthy?' into a pass/fail number, runnable in CI on a checked-in reference log, is what makes replay usable by a team without a dedicated software mentor. AdvantageKit already writes both tables into the same output file (`RealOutputs` and `ReplayOutputs`) and AdvantageScope already exports 'AdvantageKit Cycles'-aligned rows — the diff engine is the missing 20 lines of glue that nobody has written.
capabilities.prerequisites: AdvantageKit replay configured (`Logger.setReplaySource(new WPILOGReader(...))` + `WPILOGWriter(addPathSuffix(path,"_sim"))` + `setUseTiming(false)`). Read the resulting WPILOG with `edu.wpi.first.util.datalog.DataLogReader`. Simulation GUI must be disabled (already the template default).

capabilities.capability: `RootstockMechanism` — one declaration that emits Mechanism2d, 3D component Pose3d[], and measured/setpoint/goal ghost triples
capabilities.whyItMatters: This is the user's headline ask and it is currently three unrelated manual chores. AdvantageScope's own docs warn that articulated 3D components are 'complex and time-consuming'; 6328's DarwinMechanism3d is 80 lines of hand-written trig per robot, hardcoding CAD offsets and hand-composing `Transform3d`s, and they maintain a *separate* set of constants because the exported CAD differs slightly from the real robot. A small team cannot sustain that. If Rootstock lets you describe a kinematic chain once and get the 2D mechanism, the 3D component array, AND the parallel setpoint/goal arrays for free, superstructure visualization goes from a week of work to an afternoon.
capabilities.prerequisites: AdvantageKit `Logger.recordOutput(String, Pose3d...)` and `LoggedMechanism2d`. The generated component index order must be documented as the contract with `config.json` `components[]`. Ship `MechanismSpec.exportAssetConfig()` (below) so the two cannot drift.

capabilities.capability: AdvantageScope asset toolchain — in-repo robot assets, a `config.json` scaffolder, and a live calibration mode
capabilities.whyItMatters: The AdvantageScope custom-asset spec is precise but unforgiving: folder must be `Robot_NAME`, base model `model.glb` with NO components, each component a separate `model_0.glb`…`model_N.glb`, `rotations` applied before `position`, and the docs' calibration procedure is a literal six-step trial-and-error loop ('adjust the rotations, followed by the positions, for each component until they are aligned to the origin'). Every one of those steps is a place a rookie gives up. AdvantageScope already supports pointing at an arbitrary parent folder ('This feature allows custom assets to be stored under version control alongside robot code') — nobody has built the tooling around that hook.
capabilities.prerequisites: AdvantageScope 'Use Custom Assets Folder' (App menu). AdvantageKit `LoggedNetworkNumber` published under `/Tuning` (that exact table is what AdvantageScope tuning mode makes editable). Document the CAD path: Onshape -> STEP -> CAD Assistant -> .glb with 'Merge faces within the same part' enabled.

capabilities.capability: `RootstockLogSession` — competition-aware log naming, retention, routing, and a post-match triage manifest
capabilities.whyItMatters: AdvantageKit's WPILOGWriter already renames to `akit_<yy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss>_<event>_<matchtype><n>.wpilog` and WPILib names `WPILib_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss_{event}_{match}.wpilog` — but neither writes a machine-readable index, neither correlates the akit log with the .hoot folder / .revlog / DS log from the same match, and neither records alliance/station/replay-number/game-data in a place you can grep. At a competition a small team has ~6 minutes between matches. Producing a one-line-per-match manifest with 'what to look at' pre-computed is the difference between triaging and guessing.
capabilities.prerequisites: AdvantageKit auto-logs `DriverStation/{EventName,MatchType,MatchNumber,ReplayNumber,AllianceStation,GameSpecificMessage}` (verified in LoggedDriverStation.java) plus `LoggedRobot/FullCycleMS`, `Logger/QueuedCycle`, `SystemStats/*`. Metadata via `Logger.recordMetadata("GitSHA", BuildConstants.GIT_SHA)`.

capabilities.capability: `./gradlew pullLogs` — fast, indexed, resumable log retrieval + auto-open in AdvantageScope
capabilities.whyItMatters: AdvantageScope's own 2026 release notes quantify the problem: SFTP downloads ran at 25 Mb/s under high roboRIO CPU load, and moving to FTP got them to 80 Mb/s. The DataLogTool is SFTP-only and cannot connect at all while the field radio firewall is up. Today a team does this by hand, in a GUI, once per match. A one-command pull that skips already-downloaded files, groups the .hoot subfolder with its .wpilog, writes the manifest, and hands the newest log straight to AdvantageScope turns a 6-minute chore into 20 seconds.
capabilities.prerequisites: FTP (preferred, matches AdvantageScope 2026) with SFTP fallback. Robot log paths: 2026 `/U/logs` and `/home/lvuser/logs`; 2027 `/u/logs` and `/home/systemcore/logs` (user systemcore/systemcore). Must document that this cannot run while on the competition field.

capabilities.capability: Faults + Alerts + performance tracer, unified and AdvantageScope-native
capabilities.whyItMatters: DogLog has the best fault ergonomics in FRC (`logFault`/`decreaseFault`/`clearFault`, auto-raising WPILib Alerts, publishing Counts/Seen/Active arrays) and its docs correctly frame it as a post-match checklist item. AdvantageKit has the best perf instrumentation (auto `FullCycleMS`/`GCTimeMS`/`QueuedCycle`, and 6328's `LoggedTracer` idiom). Neither has both, and the DogLog docs warn you must not run both libraries. A small team needs 'the robot tells you what broke' far more than it needs another graph.
capabilities.prerequisites: AdvantageKit auto-logs WPILib persistent Alerts to the outputs table already; AdvantageScope renders them on the Line Graph tab. Use `Timer.getMonotonicTimestamp()` (NOT `getTimestamp()`) inside the tracer so replay-accelerated runs report real wall time.

capabilities.capability: Curated telemetry tiers with an FMS-aware budget (the anti-loop-overrun feature)
capabilities.whyItMatters: Every real 2026 failure I found traces to logging volume, not logging design. Teams on Chief Delphi reported 80-150ms loop times that dropped when they deleted log calls; one found the culprit was 'logger statements instantiating new Translation2ds every cycle.' DogLog's own FAQ says the same. AdvantageKit's answer — 'log it as an input and recover the rest via replay' — is correct but requires knowing which is which. Making tiers first-class, with a hard per-cycle budget that degrades gracefully on FMS, is what lets a small team log aggressively at home without bricking themselves at an event.
capabilities.prerequisites: AdvantageKit already provides `Logger.runEveryN(int, Runnable)`. Tier gating must be a compile-visible no-op, not a runtime `if` inside a method whose arguments were already computed — otherwise you pay the CAN read anyway (the exact trap the Epilogue docs describe).

capabilities.capability: Ghost-pose conventions baked into path following and superstructure goals
capabilities.whyItMatters: 'Measured vs setpoint vs goal' is the single most useful visualization in FRC and it is pure convention today — every team invents its own key names, so no shared tooling can exist. If Rootstock fixes the convention (and the PathPlanner/Choreo adapters emit it automatically), then AdvantageScope layouts, the replay-diff tool, and the auto-triage manifest can all key off it, and a rookie gets a correct 2D-field view with a target ghost on day one.
capabilities.prerequisites: `Logger.recordOutput(String, Pose2d...)` / struct publishers. AdvantageScope ghost + trajectory object types on the 2D/3D field tabs. Coordinate system must be declared: blue-wall for 2023-2026, center/red starting 2027.

capabilities.whyItMatters: WPILib 2027 moves every Java package from `edu.wpi.first.*` to `org.wpilib.*`, renames `frc::`->`wpi::`, DELETES Shuffleboard and SmartDashboard, adds Commands v3, renames Test mode to Utility, replaces XboxController/PS4Controller/etc with a single Gamepad class, drops NT3, and moves the FRC field origin to field-center. AdvantageKit's 2027 line already imports `org.wpilib.*` and its docs state '2027 templates are not currently available.' DogLog has already shipped 2027.1.0 against alpha-5. If Rootstock's public API leaks WPILib types raw, it breaks entirely; if it wraps the volatile surfaces, Rootstock becomes the thing that absorbs the 2027 shock for its users — a very strong adoption argument for a small team.
capabilities.prerequisites: Track allwpilib 2027 alphas (currently v2027.0.0-alpha-6) and AdvantageKit v27.0.0-alpha-4. Do NOT ship 2027 support in the first release — ship the *facade* now so the migration is cheap later.

eliteTeamPractices: FRC 6328 log EVERY subsystem behind an IO interface with `@AutoLog` inputs, then call exactly two lines per cycle: `io.updateInputs(inputs); Logger.processInputs("ExampleSubsystem", inputs);` — and the subsystem then reads from the inputs object, never from the IO layer, so the cache is never updated mid-cycle. That single rule is what makes replay byte-identical. https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/recording-inputs/io-interfaces

6328's 2026 robot (Darwin) records full provenance metadata at construction — `ProjectName`, `BuildDate`, `GitSHA`, `GitDate`, `GitBranch`, a `GitDirty` string ('All changes committed' / 'Uncommitted changes'), `Hostname`, and a formatted `Platform` string — so any log can be traced to an exact commit. https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/Robot.java

6328 log command lifecycle by hooking the scheduler: `onCommandInitialize/onCommandFinish/onCommandInterrupt` write both `CommandsUnique/<name>_<hashcode>` (per-instance boolean) and `CommandsAll/<name>` (reference-counted boolean). This is how you find a command that got interrupted in match 42. Same file as above.

6328 instrument the loop with a hand-rolled tracer that uses `Timer.getFPGATimestamp()` (the real clock, not the replay clock) and emits `LoggedTracer/<epoch>MS`, called at `Robot/Commands`, `Robot/AfterScheduler`, `ObjectDetection/ClearOldFuelPoses`, and `Robot/Periodic`. https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/util/LoggedTracer.java

6328's 3D mechanism visualization is a dedicated singleton (`DarwinMechanism3d`) whose only public method is `log(String key)`. It holds setter-driven state (`hoodAngle`, `intakeAngle`, `trashCompactorHeight`), computes each component `Pose3d` by composing `Transform3d`s from CAD-derived constants, emits them as one varargs call `Logger.recordOutput(key + "/Components", hoodPose, intakePose, frontHopperPose, trashCompactorPose)`, and separately emits `key + "/Camera"` as a field-relative camera pose for AdvantageScope's Camera Override. Critically, they keep a SEPARATE set of constants from `VisionConstants` because 'these values may differ ... as they are calibrated for the version of the CAD exported for use in AdvantageScope.' https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/DarwinMechanism3d.java

Elite teams suppress NetworkTables publishing when FMS-attached. 6328 ship a custom `NoFMSNT4Publisher` in place of the stock `NT4Publisher` on the real robot. DogLog does the analogous thing by default: `ntTunables` is ignored when connected to FMS. https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/Robot.java and https://doglog.dev/reference/configuring

6328 compress logs on the robot — they run `WPILOGXZWriter`/`WPILOGXZReader` (xz-compressed `.wpilogxz`) as the real-robot data receiver and decompress transparently for replay, with a `WPILOGExtractor` utility. This is a non-obvious, high-value trick for USB stick capacity and download time that no library exposes. https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/tree/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/util/logging

Tunables go under the `/Tuning` NetworkTables table and nowhere else, because AdvantageScope's tuning mode makes exactly that table editable while `NetworkInputs` (AdvantageKit's replay-record table) is read-only: `new LoggedNetworkNumber("/Tuning/MyTunableNumber", 0.0)`. https://docs.advantagescope.org/overview/live-sources/tuning-mode

Teams using DogLog extend it rather than accept the defaults: 4522 (Team SCREAM) extend it to log different fields at different frequencies specifically to minimize loop times; 3847 (Spectrum) wrap it in a `Telemetry` class adding priority levels and Command logging; 9496 (LYNK) log a single high-level superstructure state field so the whole robot's logic is readable as one trace. https://doglog.dev/getting-started/faq

The high-value replay workflow is additive logging, not code modification. Per @Programming4907 on Chief Delphi: 'you can pull the log from the robot after a practice session or a match, and if you wondered what this one internal variable was doing, you could add a line to log that variable, rebuild, log replay, and then view the new log in AdvantageScope ... I think that's the real power of log replay that doesn't get enough recognition.' AdvantageKit's maintainer (@jonahb55) adds the second one: 'you can use the debugger during replay.' https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/doglog-vs-advantage-kit/508842

Elite teams run `./gradlew replayWatch`, which re-runs replay and refreshes AdvantageScope on every save to `src`, preserving the time range and visualization layout across reloads. Combined with `setUseTiming(false)` (replay at ~50x real time with zero accuracy loss) this makes 'add a log line, see the answer' a sub-10-second loop. https://docs.advantagekit.org/getting-started/replay-watch

Timestamps are recorded per-measurement, not read from the clock. The recommended pattern is to take the timestamp from the source — NetworkTables subscriber timestamps or Phoenix 6 `StatusSignal.SignalMeasurement.timestamp` — and feed those into the pose estimator, rather than calling any timer inside the control loop. https://docs.advantagekit.org/theory/deterministic-timestamps

Custom robot assets live under version control alongside robot code via AdvantageScope's 'Use Custom Assets Folder', which takes a parent folder containing multiple `TYPE_NAME` subfolders. https://docs.advantagescope.org/more-features/custom-assets

Post-match fault review is treated as a checklist, not an ad-hoc activity: 'Just like how having post-match checklists for physical maintenance improve reliability, checking the logs after matches helps catch software issues that otherwise may go unnoticed.' https://doglog.dev/reference/faults

Game-piece animation is used to make auto routines legible — 6328's KitBot example animates a note traveling from robot to speaker as part of the actual launch sequence command, and beam-break state makes a game piece appear inside the robot in the 3D view. https://docs.advantagescope.org/tab-reference/3d-field/
pitfalls: AdvantageKit CPU cost is real and bit many teams in 2026. On https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/loop-overruns-with-advantage-kit/516167 multiple teams using the stock TalonFX-Swerve + Vision templates reported ~0.08s average loops, 100-150ms spikes, and one case of 0.5-0.6s vision periodic — bad enough that 'we could push a button and nothing would happen, but several seconds later the subsystem would briefly run.' Documented fixes: delete unneeded log calls (one team found 'the logger statements were instantiating new Translation2ds every cycle'), stop logging vision summary fields and per-tag poses, and drop the template's 250 Hz odometry thread to 150-200 Hz. One team's root cause was simply that `simMode` was still set to SIMBOT, so vision simulation was running on the real robot.

AdvantageKit's maintainer's diagnostic order, from https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/advantage-kit-logging-cause-lag-in-roborio/516409 : check `RealOutputs/LoggedRobot/*` cycle times first, then `RealOutputs/Logger/QueuedCycles` — 'queue overflows only tend to occur in cases where data is being produced faster than the disk can write it, or where data is being flushed too infrequently by custom log receivers.' If CPU is pegged, `ssh lvuser@10.XX.XX.2` and run `top`; 6328 have seen a roboRIO FPGA-interrupt issue with USB-stick logging that presents identically. Per-cycle `log.flush()` from the background receiver thread is intentional, not a bug.

Protobuf values, custom records, and any new struct type can block **>100 ms on first log**. AdvantageKit's docs mark this :::danger and mandate: 'Protobuf values should always be logged for the first time when the robot is disabled.' Same warning applies to record logging. This will absolutely cause a match-start loop overrun if you first log a record inside an auto command. https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/supported-types

Record classes must be globally uniquely named — 'Logging multiple record types of the same name can cause conflicts' — and record fields may not be arrays. Use multiple top-level record arrays instead. Same source.

`Timer.getMonotonicTimestamp()` / `RobotController.getMonotonicTime()` return the REAL FPGA clock and are unaffected by replay. Using them in control logic silently destroys replay fidelity; using `Timer.getTimestamp()` for performance measurement gives you nonsense during accelerated replay. The rule: monotonic inside IO impls and profilers only. https://docs.advantagekit.org/theory/deterministic-timestamps
`DriverStation.waitForDsConnection()` is flatly incompatible with AdvantageKit. https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/built-in-logging

The 'replay bubble': modified outputs cannot affect replayed inputs. You can add outputs and re-derive them, but you cannot make the replayed robot take a different action and see what would have happened — the inputs are frozen. Teams who expect a what-if simulator will be disappointed. https://docs.advantagekit.org/getting-started/traditional-replay
The simulation GUI must be DISABLED for replay to work (it is off by default in the AdvantageKit templates, so this only bites people wiring replay into an existing project). Same source.

Vendor CAN loggers are decorative from replay's perspective. AdvantageKit's own URCL page says it outright: 'URCL compatibility with AdvantageKit is provided for convenience only; the data recorded to the log is NOT available in replay. REV motor controllers must still be part of an IO implementation with defined inputs to support replay.' The same is true of CTRE hoot logs. https://docs.advantagescope.org/more-features/urcl

Since 2025 REVLib, most Spark status frames are DISABLED by default until an associated getter is called — so URCL/StatusLogger will silently omit any signal you never read. You must configure `SignalsConfig` explicitly to get them in the log. Same source.

Hoot Replay's non-determinism is not a theoretical concern. 6328 published real 2025 log data showing that at 5x real-time with hand-added compensation code (a best case), robot state 'completely diverged between real and replay' within a few seconds of auto start, and even a compensated 2x run 'breaks down completely midway through the match.' Worse, 'there is no way to distinguish accurate outputs from the inaccurate, diverged outputs' — the replay looks plausible while being wrong. https://docs.advantagekit.org/theory/log-replay-comparison

Epilogue silently will not log `Mechanism2d` ('will not be logged as they do not implement the Sendable interface in a way that is compatible with annotation logging'), and it uses the DECLARED type of a field, not the runtime type — so an IO-interface-typed field logs with the interface's config even when a rich implementation is assigned. Null fields or null-returning methods throw NPE into your error handler. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/telemetry/robot-telemetry-with-annotations.html

Do not run two logging libraries at once. DogLog's docs: 'While it may technically be possible to use DogLog in combination with other logging libraries, this is definitely not recommended. You will almost certainly encounter bugs or other compatibility issues as a result.' https://doglog.dev/getting-started/faq

`DogLogOptions.withCaptureDs(true)` cannot be turned off once enabled, and DS/joystick and console capture 'can't be published over NetworkTables' due to a `DataLogManager` limitation. https://doglog.dev/reference/configuring

WPILib `LogEntry.append()` does NO change detection — 'Every call to a LogEntry.append() function will result in a record being written to the data log.' Dedup is the caller's problem. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/telemetry/datalog.html

roboRIO USB sticks must be FAT32; NTFS/exFAT will not work, and Windows won't format >32 GB as FAT32, so use a 32 GB or smaller stick. DataLogManager deletes `WPILib_` logs oldest-first when free space drops below 50 MB (floor of 10 files); Phoenix 6 SignalLogger deletes at 50 MB free and stops logging entirely at 5 MB. Same source + CTRE signal-logging docs.

You cannot pull logs off the robot while it is on the competition field — 'The downloader uses SSH, so it will not be able to connect wirelessly if the radio firewall is enabled.' Plan the workflow around tethering in the pit, not around field access. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/telemetry/datalog-download.html

AdvantageScope custom-asset gotchas, all silent failures: folder must be exactly `TYPE_NAME` (`Robot_`/`Field2d_`/`Field3d_`/`Joystick_`); base `model.glb` must contain NO components; components must be `model_0.glb`, `model_1.glb`, … in the same order as `config.json`'s `components[]`; `rotations` are applied BEFORE `position`; the origin of component poses is the published robot pose, which is normally at FLOOR height (z=0), not the bellypan; and AdvantageScope auto-simplifies geometry (escape hatches: put `NOSIMPLIFY` in a mesh name, or set `"disableSimplification": true`). https://docs.advantagescope.org/more-features/custom-assets

The AdvantageKit docs contain a method-name typo. `docs/data-flow/supported-types.md` shows `mechanism.generate3dMechanisms()` (plural) but the actual v26.0.2 source declares `public synchronized ArrayList<Pose3d> generate3dMechanism()` (singular). Verified in akit/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/junction/mechanism/LoggedMechanism2d.java at tag v26.0.2. Do not copy the docs snippet.

AdvantageKit mechanism logging requires the `LoggedMechanism2d` family, not WPILib's `Mechanism2d`. Using the WPILib classes with `Logger.recordOutput` will not compile. And unless you use `@AutoLogOutput`, `Logger.recordOutput(key, mech)` snapshots only the current state, so it must be called every cycle. https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/supported-types

AdvantageScope's 2026 FRC field model matches the WELDED field's AprilTag layout; visualizing poses computed from the AndyMark layout can be off by ~0.5 inch. https://docs.advantagescope.org/tab-reference/3d-field/

AdvantageScope video sync auto-detection only works on match videos WITH score overlays, requires FFmpeg on PATH (auto-download only on Windows/macOS; Linux users must install it manually), needs a TBA API key for the Blue Alliance lookup, and produces no audio because frames are transcoded. YouTube/TBA download can break without warning when YouTube changes. https://docs.advantagescope.org/tab-reference/video

Exporting log data from AdvantageScope for SysId is lossy unless you pick the right options — use the 'AdvantageKit Cycles' timestamp mode for AdvantageKit logs, and never export SIMULATION-generated data for SysId at all. For URCL SysId you MUST export with 'Include Generated' before the analyzer can read it. https://docs.advantagescope.org/overview/log-files/export

2027 will break everything, and the alphas are already public. Java `edu.wpi.first.*` -> `org.wpilib.*`; C++ `frc::` -> `wpi::`; **Shuffleboard and SmartDashboard are REMOVED**; NT3 removed; PathWeaver and RobotBuilder removed; Test mode renamed Utility; `MotorController.set()` -> `setThrottle()`; XboxController/PS4Controller/PS5Controller/StadiaController collapse into one `Gamepad`; Commands v3 added; relay/analog-out/SPI removed. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html

The FRC field coordinate system CHANGES in 2027: origin moves to field center with +X facing away from the RED alliance wall ('center/red', the Systemcore default). Blue-wall origin is 2023-2026 only. Any hardcoded field geometry, mirroring util, or asset config with `"coordinateSystem": "wall-blue"` becomes wrong. https://docs.advantagescope.org/more-features/coordinate-systems

AdvantageScope Lite and the `localhost:6768/ascope` endpoint are 2027-only. Quote from the live docs: 'AdvantageScope Lite is only available in the 2027 (v27.x) releases of AdvantageScope on the Systemcore control system.' Do not design a 2026 feature around it. https://docs.advantagescope.org/more-features/advantagescope-lite
AdvantageKit 2027 templates do not exist yet — 'Template projects are not currently available for the 2027 alpha versions.' https://docs.advantagekit.org/getting-started/installation/

Legacy AdvantageKit projects (v4.0.0-beta-1 and earlier) will fail to build until the GitHub Packages maven block in build.gradle is replaced with `maven { url = uri("https://frcmaven.wpi.edu/artifactory/littletonrobotics-mvn-release") }`. Same source.

Monologue is abandoned. Last repo push 2024-06-21, last release v1.0.0-beta6 (2024-03-09), no 2025/2026/2027 vendordep. Any tutorial or team template still referencing it is stale. https://github.com/shueja/Monologue

AdvantageScope XR is iOS/iPadOS only with no plans for other platforms, needs the host firewall disabled, supports only one host session at a time, and does not render heatmaps or swerve module velocities. https://docs.advantagescope.org/tab-reference/3d-field/advantagescope-xr

Struct/protobuf serialization is the ONLY good way to publish geometry — field-name suffix parsing is AdvantageScope's third-choice fallback ('🥉'). If you publish a raw double named `armAngle` with no unit metadata and no suffix, AdvantageScope cannot label or convert it. Use struct types, or `Logger.recordOutput(key, value, Meters)`, or name it `armAngleRad`. https://docs.advantagescope.org/tab-reference/line-graph/units
